_meta.source: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements – Pregnancy (Health Professional Fact Sheet)
_meta.description: Nutrient intake recommendations (RDA/AI) and Upper Limits (UL) during pregnancy, directly from the NIH ODS fact sheet Tables 1 and 2.
notes: Bolded values in the original table indicate the intake recommendation is HIGHER during pregnancy vs nonpregnant females.
For folate, magnesium, niacin, and vitamin E, the ULs apply only to supplemental intakes, not food.
For vitamin A, the UL applies only to preformed vitamin A (retinol), not beta-carotene.
ND = Not Determinable (insufficient data for UL).

calcium.note: 21.2% of pregnant women in US have dietary calcium intakes below EAR. Supplementation of 1500-2000 mg/day may reduce preeclampsia risk.

choline.note: AI increases to 450 mg. Most pregnant women in US do not consume recommended amount. Less than half of prenatal supplements contain choline.

folate.note: RDA increases to 600 mcg DFE. 35.8% of pregnant women below EAR. 400-800 mcg/day folic acid recommended before/during conception. High-risk NTD: 4000-5000 mcg/day. Only folic acid (not 5-MTHF) proven to reduce NTD risk.

iodine.note: RDA increases to 220 mcg. Median dietary intake 216 mcg/day among pregnant US women. Many organizations recommend 150 mcg/day iodine supplement during pregnancy.

iron.note: RDA increases to 27 mg. 83.8% of pregnant US women have dietary intake below EAR. 27.9% exceed UL when food+supplements combined. Routine supplementation in iron-replete women may have adverse effects.

magnesium.note: RDA increases to 400 (14-18), 350 (19-30), 360 (31-50). 53.3% of pregnant US women below EAR. UL of 350 mg applies to supplemental magnesium only.

omega3_dha_epa.note: ALA AI increases to 1.4 g. No formal DRI for DHA/EPA. Expert groups recommend 8-12 oz seafood/week. At least 250 mg/day DHA+EPA from diet/supplements, plus additional 100-200 mg/day DHA during pregnancy. Cochrane review supports omega-3 for preterm birth risk reduction.
omega3_dha_epa.expert_rec_dha_epa_mg: 250 mg/day DHA+EPA minimum, plus 100-200 mg DHA extra in pregnancy

vitamin_a.note: RDA increases to 750 (14-18) or 770 (19-50) mcg RAE. 27.7% below EAR. UL applies to PREFORMED vitamin A only (not beta-carotene). Excessive preformed vitamin A is teratogenic.

vitamin_b6.note: RDA increases to 1.9 mg. 25.4% below EAR. Helps reduce nausea/vomiting in pregnancy. EFSA sets UL at 12 mg/day (vs US 80-100 mg).

vitamin_b12.note: RDA increases to 2.6 mcg. Most US pregnant women have sufficient intake. Vegans/vegetarians at higher risk of deficiency. No UL established.

vitamin_d.note: RDA is 15 mcg. ~90% of US pregnant women have intake below EAR. May reduce preeclampsia risk. UL is 100 mcg/day.

zinc.note: RDA increases to 12 (14-18) or 11 (19-50) mg. 21.5% below EAR. Effects of supplementation on pregnancy outcomes unclear.
